Home / Services / Material reception & intake
08 / RECEPTION

A clear intake creates a traceable beginning.

The first point of receipt is where a material description becomes an identifiable consignment or specimen record. A thoughtful reception plan considers what is expected, what physically arrives and what information should follow the material.

THE SERVICE IN CONTEXT

A defined scope leads to a better decision.

Understand how identification, declared weight, condition and specimen records fit together.

The suitable approach depends on the material, the intended outcome and the details agreed by the parties.

Make a service enquiry ↗
A CLOSER LOOK

What deserves attention.

Different specimen forms and questions call for different considerations. The following themes help frame the discussion.

01

Before material arrives

An advance description can include the sender, declared material type, packaging, sample count, approximate weight, intended work and supporting documents. For sensitive materials, parties should discuss acceptance conditions before dispatch.

02

Inspection, reconciliation and identification

At the point of receipt, the condition of seals and packaging, piece count and identifying marks can be checked against supplied information. Any differences should be documented and clarified before subsequent processing.

03

Weighing, sampling and next steps

Appropriate weighing, sample separation and unique identifiers can support a coherent chain of records. The path thereafter may involve examination, processing, storage, return or commercial discussion, depending on an agreed scope.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

What to prepare.

A few useful details can make your first enquiry much more focused.

  • Sender and authorised recipient details
  • Material category, form and approximate weight
  • Number of packages and sample identifiers
  • Packaging and seal information, if relevant
  • Prior analyses, consignment records or safety notes
Explore preparation guides ↗
COMMON QUESTIONS

A little more clarity.

Is reception the same as an assay?+
No. Reception establishes what was received and how it is identified; analysis or examination is a separate activity.
Should I ship material before speaking to ASL?+
Contact ASL first to agree on suitability, any acceptance conditions and handover arrangements.
